summary.headline: Vijaya Diagnostic Q4 FY26 revenue rose 26.6% YoY to INR 219 crore and EBITDA margin hit 43.5%, with FY27 margin guided at 40%+.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 26.6% YoY to INR 219 crore on 18.5% test volume growth, with the balance from test mix. EBITDA rose 38.7% to INR 95.5 crore (43.5% margin, up 379 bps), and PAT rose 37.5% to INR 47.9 crore. For FY26, revenue reached INR 814 crore (up 19.5%), EBITDA INR 337 crore (41.4% margin) and PAT INR 173 crore (21.2% margin). Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to "40%" while signalling it would aim higher, and planned 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes with INR 140-150 crore capex.

financial_highlights.change: Management attributed rise to new hub ramp-up mix

segments.name: Geography (Q4 revenue share)
segments.commentary: Hyderabad 67%, rest of AP/Telangana 20%, Pune (PH) 6%, West Bengal 4%, others 3%. Hyderabad grew ~20% YoY in Q4, a key driver of operating leverage.

segments.name: Pathology vs radiology
segments.commentary: Radiology was 37% of revenue; B2C was 92%. Both pathology and radiology drove growth.

segments.name: Pune (PH Diagnostics)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 16% YoY in Q4 (footfall ~15%), after Q3 growth of ~8%; Ambegaon hub reached breakeven in one year. Kalyani Nagar hub also opened in Q2 FY26.

segments.name: Wellness
segments.commentary: Growth consistently around 30%; packages roughly 50:50 radiology and pathology; average realisation INR 1,800-2,000 per patient, retail above INR 2,500.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: HSR and Yelahanka hubs (opened Q1 FY26): Yelahanka reached breakeven, HSR close to breakeven. Bannerghatta flagship with PET-CT, cardiac CT and wide-bore MRI expected ready in a couple of months.

segments.name: Kolkata / West Bengal
segments.commentary: 7 hubs in Kolkata; VIP Road grew double digits YoY; two Q1 FY26 hubs broke even in under 9 months; three newer centres (incl. Phoolbagan, Diamond Harbour) targeted for breakeven within a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 40%+, with management saying it would be conservative and aim for better; company says it can deliver 30%+ even while opening new centres.

FY27 capex INR 140-150 crore for new centres and the automated lab; INR 120-130 crore for 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes from executed leases, plus automated lab in Panjagutta, Hyderabad; includes INR 10-12 crore replacement capex.
FY27 maintenance capex INR 10-15 crore, roughly 2-2.5% of topline.
Price hike of 1-1.5% planned, likely Q1 or Q2 FY27, on selected tests; realisation growth of 1-1.5% expected, with focus on volume growth over the next 2-3 years.
Pune expected to grow double digit in FY27 and to double revenue in 3-5 years; Hyderabad expected to grow double digit over 2-3 years.
Capex guidance to be revisited quarterly as new leases are executed; Bangalore, Pune, Kolkata or other geographies may add centres.
Genomics described as long-term play with no significant revenue in next few years; to be run from one central lab in Hyderabad.
capex_capacity: FY27 plan: 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes across network, with new fully automated lab at Panjagutta, Hyderabad with automated track system to improve turnaround time.

Network at call: ~50 hubs, ~112 spokes, 30 labs (including mini labs); 162 centres in total; ~95 in Hyderabad, ~35 in rest of AP/Telangana, 7 in Kolkata, 2 in Bangalore, 1 each in Gulbarga and Gurgaon, balance in Pune.
Two Pune hubs (Ambegaon and Kalyani Nagar) and two spokes opened recently; Pune capacity is a constraint in some PH centres, with existing-centre growth in low single digits.
Management is not pursuing North India for now; Gurgaon is a single wellness centre, and expansion focus is Karnataka and West Bengal for 3-5 years.
Inorganic: 8-15 assets come up each year; management will only add a large acquisition if it is B2C-driven, valuation-reasonable and of sufficient size.
demand_pricing: Hyderabad growth of ~20% in Q4 attributed to favourable season, market share gains and network expansion; management says it matches market rates, perhaps 2-3% higher.
Hospital-based labs compete; management says Vijaya is 20-25% cheaper than hospitals and differentiates on large format centres of 6,000-8,000 sq ft and integrated pathology and radiology.
Corporate wellness churn seen from price-sensitive corporates and aggregators; large corporate relationships continuing for 2-3 years; online players seen as having limited impact.
No GLP-1 (weight-loss drug) test-volume impact visible yet; requests for GLP packages not yet seen.

Management says revenue-per-test rise was driven by new hubs ramping up with radiology-heavy mix in first year; increase in wellness packages would raise revenue per patient but lower revenue per test.
Digital marketing spend of INR 6-7 crore in FY26 expected to double in FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin outperformance in Q4 (43.5%) given other expenses grew 21%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base and new hubs breaking even faster than expected; Hyderabad growth of 20% helped. New-centre OPEX burn for FY26 was about 0.8% against the 2-2.5% envisaged. Incremental costs in talent and technology will continue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margin accretion be sharper given spoke-heavy additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margins may be similar to FY26 with 12 spokes and 4 hubs; more hubs would be a bigger drag. Guidance is 40%, with an aim to do better.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 280-300 crore cash be deployed, and what about M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will consider B2C-driven, same-ethos assets at reasonable valuations, with 8-15 opportunities a year. Capex guidance covers only executed leases and will be updated quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of the INR 150 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 120-130 crore for 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes from executed leases, plus the automated lab; includes INR 10-12 crore replacement capex.

qa_highlights.question: Pune hub ramp-up and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Both new Pune hubs have taken similar time; Ambegaon broke even in one year and Kalyani Nagar is expected to take a full year. Pune growth was slow after acquisition due to integration and culture work; management expects revenue to double in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Competition from hospital-based labs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hospital labs focus on in-patients and fasting OPD tests, and Vijaya's 20-25% lower prices and integrated large-format centres differentiate it; Bangalore has no large integrated player.

risks_watch: FY27 margin could compress if more hubs (versus spokes) open, since new hubs carry higher ramp-up costs; management said the 40% guide is conservative.
Pune growth is still low-to-mid-teens and depends on capacity additions and the corporate segment; management has previously missed its Pune targets.
Corporate wellness churn from price-sensitive clients and aggregators; wellness repeat-customer data has only been tracked for about two years.
Genomics and AI investments are early; AI tools need regulatory validation, and CRM/ERP rollouts are due in FY27 after an earlier LIMS hiccup.
Quarterly updates on capex and centre count promised; watch for executed leases and any large M&A deal.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, margins and network expansion, with careful guidance: management is explicitly conservative on the 40% margin and hedges on capex and M&A pending executed leases. It was less specific on Genomics, AI and GLP-1 demand, which it described as early or unquantified.
key_quotes: So, it's basically the operating leverage in the existing network.
So we're saying you have entire Pune and then Calcutta and now already Bangalore is a new baby and with a few more hubs coming there.
Genomics is a long-term play. I don't think we'll see any significant revenue coming in the next years.
we're very confident that in next three to five years, we'll be easily doubling up our revenue from where we are now.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin at 40%+ and 1-1.5% realisation growth, backed by 4-5 hubs, 10-12 spokes and an automated Hyderabad lab on INR 140-150 crore capex from executed leases, though no FY27 revenue growth number was given and utilisation was described only as a little constrained.
